name: analytics
purpose: Turns the event stream into answers: event ingestion, daily rollups, funnels, cohorts, retention curves and the admin KPI dashboards. It reads events; it never writes to another module's data.
businessPurpose: Product decisions in a learning platform are only as good as the retention and outcome data behind them. This module exists so that "does this feature help people learn?" is answerable with numbers rather than opinion.
responsibilities: Event ingestion from the outbox into an analytics store
Daily and weekly rollups by learner, cohort, skill and level
Funnels: signup → placement → first lesson → day-7 return → subscription
Retention curves and cohort analysis
Learning outcome metrics: level progression, review accuracy, band improvement
AI cost per active learner
Admin KPI dashboards and scheduled reports
The weekly learner progress email payload
notResponsibilities: Operational metrics — that is Prometheus and `platform/telemetry`
Owning the source data — it derives, never mutates

tables.name: daily_rollups
tables.notes: `date`, `dimension`, `dimension_value`, `metric`, `value`. The read path for every dashboard.

consumes.reason: Every domain event is ingested; this module is the one legitimate universal subscriber

dependsWhy.job: Ingestion, rollups and reports are scheduled work

rules: Analytics derives; it never writes to another module's tables. If it needs a fact, the fact must arrive as an event.
Ingestion is idempotent on `event_id` — at-least-once delivery must not inflate counts.
Dashboards read rollups, never raw events. A dashboard query that scans `analytics_events` is a bug.
Rollups are recomputable: a late or replayed event triggers a recompute of the affected day rather than an in-place adjustment.
Personal data in analytics is minimised — user IDs, never names or emails; free-text content is never ingested.
A deleted user's events are anonymised to a synthetic ID so aggregate history stays truthful while the person disappears.
Learner-facing insights are computed from the same rollups the admin dashboards use, so the two can never disagree.
Every metric has a written definition in `docs/product/metrics.md`; an undefined metric on a dashboard is not allowed, because two people will interpret it differently.
Cohort membership is immutable once assigned — a learner's signup week does not change.

errors.meaning: Requested range exceeds the query limit
The requested day has not been rolled up yet

security: Analytics access requires a specific permission and is audited.
Exports are delivered by short-lived signed URL and are logged.
No free-text learner content is ever ingested — not essay bodies, not transcripts.

flows.title: Ingestion to dashboard
flows.mermaid:
flowchart LR A[Domain events via outbox] --> B[ingest job
idempotent on event_id] B --> C[(analytics_events
partitioned, append-only)] C --> D[nightly rollup job] D --> E[(daily_rollups)] E --> F[KPI / funnel / retention queries] F --> G[cache 15 min] G --> H[admin dashboard] E --> I[learner insights] E --> J[weekly progress email] K[late or replayed event] --> L[mark the day dirty] --> D

tasks.title: Add a metric
steps: Write its definition in `docs/product/metrics.md` first — including what it excludes.
Confirm the source event carries the properties needed; if not, extend the event (a versioned change).
Add the rollup computation and backfill historical days with a job.
Add a test with a known dataset and a hand-computed expected value.

limitations: Rollups are nightly, so dashboards are up to a day stale for anything not also computed live.
There is no real-time analytics path; Prometheus covers operational immediacy.
Everything lives in the same PostgreSQL instance — at high volume this becomes the first candidate for a separate analytical store.
testFocus: Ingestion idempotency under duplicate delivery
Rollup recomputation on a late event
Cohort immutability
Anonymisation on user deletion preserves aggregate totals
Dashboard queries hit rollups, asserted by a query-plan test
Metric values match hand-computed expectations on a fixture dataset

decisions.question: Same database or a separate analytical store?
decisions.why: A second datastore adds a synchronisation problem and operational burden that our volume does not justify; the rollup design means moving later is a change of destination, not of pipeline

decisions.question: Ingest content?
decisions.why: Essay and transcript text would turn an analytics store into a second copy of the most sensitive data we hold, for no analytical benefit that aggregate metrics do not already provide

todo.title: Phase 4
items: Event ingestion with idempotency and partitioning
Nightly rollup job with dirty-day recomputation

doNot: Do not query another module's tables — consume events.
Do not run a dashboard query against raw events.
Do not ingest learner free text.
Do not add a metric without a written definition.
Do not mutate a rollup in place — recompute the day.

name: subscription
purpose: Plans, entitlements and the subscription lifecycle: trials, upgrades, downgrades, renewals, grace periods and cancellation. It decides what a learner is allowed to do; `payment` decides whether money moved.
context: Entitlements are read on nearly every AI-consuming request, so they are cached aggressively and invalidated eagerly. The separation from `payment` matters: a gateway outage must not change what an existing subscriber can do.
responsibilities: Plan catalogue with prices and entitlements
Entitlement resolution: what this learner may do right now
Subscription lifecycle and state transitions
Trials, upgrades, downgrades and proration rules
Renewal scheduling and grace periods on failed payment
Cancellation and reactivation
Feature gating helpers used by other modules
notResponsibilities: Enforcing a quota in the moment — the consuming module does that using the entitlement

tables.name: entitlements
tables.notes: `plan_id`, `key` (e.g. `ai.writing.daily`), `value`. A missing key means not entitled

endpoints.purpose: Start a subscription or trial (delegates checkout to `payment`)

contract.name: subscription.EntitlementReader
contract.purpose: `Entitlement(ctx, userID, key) (value, bool)` — the single question every gated feature asks

rules: Entitlements are resolved from the **subscription state**, never from payment status directly — a gateway outage must not de-entitle a paying learner.
A missing entitlement key means not entitled. Defaults are explicit in the free plan, never implicit in code.
Entitlement changes take effect within 60 seconds; the cache TTL and eager invalidation together guarantee it.
One active subscription per learner.
An upgrade is immediate with proration; a downgrade takes effect at the period end, so a learner never loses paid-for capability early.
A failed renewal enters a grace period (default 7 days) with full access, then downgrades to free — access is not cut off the moment a card fails.
Cancellation is always at period end; a mid-period refund is a `payment` decision, handled separately.
A trial requires no payment method and converts only with explicit consent — no silent charge at trial end.
Complimentary grants require a reason and are audited.
Downgrading never deletes learner data; it only restricts what can be created going forward.

errors.meaning: The feature requires a higher plan

stateMachine.description: Grace exists so that a card expiring does not immediately take away a paying learner's access. Every transition writes a `subscription_events` row.
stateMachine.mermaid:
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Free
    Free --> Trialing: start a trial
    Trialing --> Active: converts with consent
    Trialing --> Free: trial ends without conversion
    Free --> Active: subscribe
    Active --> Active: renewal succeeds
    Active --> Grace: renewal payment fails
    Grace --> Active: payment recovered
    Grace --> Free: grace expires
    Active --> PendingCancel: cancel at period end
    PendingCancel --> Active: reactivate
    PendingCancel --> Free: period ends
    Active --> Free: refunded in full

flows.title: Entitlement check on an AI feature
flows.mermaid:
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor U as Learner
    participant W as writing
    participant S as subscription
    participant C as Redis
    participant AI as platform/ai

    U->>W: POST /writing/submissions
    W->>S: Entitlement(user, "ai.writing.daily")
    S->>C: cached entitlements?
    alt miss
        S->>S: resolve from subscription + plan
        S->>C: cache 60s
    end
    S-->>W: { value: 8 }
    W->>AI: check today's usage against 8
    alt over the limit
        W-->>U: 429 AI_QUOTA_EXCEEDED with an upgrade prompt
    else within
        W->>W: proceed with submission
    end

tasks.title: Add an entitlement
steps: Choose a key following `<domain>.<feature>.<unit>` and document it in `docs/product/entitlements.md`.
Add values for every plan, including free — an absent key means not entitled, so being explicit avoids accidental gating.
Read it through `EntitlementReader` in the consuming module; never hard-code a plan name.
Add the upgrade prompt copy for the denied case.
Test the free, trial, paid and grace states.

limitations: One subscription per learner; there are no add-ons or metered top-ups in Phase 4.
Proration follows a simple day-count model rather than the gateway's own proration engine.
Currency is single per plan; multi-currency pricing is not modelled.
No family or group plans — that would edge towards the multi-tenancy the product deliberately avoids.
testFocus: Entitlement resolution across free, trial, active, grace and pending-cancel
Cache invalidation within the 60-second promise
Grace period entry and recovery
Upgrade immediate, downgrade deferred
Trial cannot be reused
Downgrade restricts creation but destroys nothing
Complimentary grants are audited with a reason

decisions.question: Entitlements from subscription state or from payment?
decisions.why: It decouples access from the gateway's availability and makes complimentary grants, trials and grace periods expressible without faking a payment

decisions.question: Cut off access immediately on a failed payment?
decisions.why: Most renewal failures are expired cards, not intent to churn; cutting access instantly converts a fixable billing problem into a lost learner

decisions.question: Downgrade immediately or at period end?
decisions.why: The learner paid for the period; taking capability away early is both unfair and a support burden

todo.title: Phase 4
items: Plans and entitlements with a seeded free tier
Subscription lifecycle with the full state machine
Entitlement resolution with caching and eager invalidation
Upgrade with proration, downgrade at period end
Grace period handling on payment failure
Upgrade prompts wherever a feature is gated

doNot: Do not read payment status to decide access.
Do not hard-code a plan name in a feature check — read an entitlement key.
Do not delete learner data on downgrade.
Do not convert a trial without explicit consent.
Do not grant a complimentary period without a recorded reason.

name: payment
purpose: Money: gateway adapters, hosted checkout sessions, webhook processing, invoices, refunds and reconciliation. Card data never touches our systems — the gateway's hosted fields do, which keeps PCI scope minimal.
context: The provider is not yet chosen (plan review Q1: VNPay/MoMo for Vietnam, Stripe for international). Everything here is written against an adapter interface so that decision is a configuration change plus one adapter file.
responsibilities: Gateway adapters behind one interface
Checkout session creation and redirect handling
Webhook receipt, signature verification, idempotent processing and replay
Payment and invoice records
Refunds, partial and full
Reconciliation between our records and the gateway's
Dunning: retry schedule and communications on failed renewals
notResponsibilities: Deciding what access a payment buys — that is `subscription`
Holding card data — the gateway does, and we never proxy it

endpoints.purpose: Create a hosted checkout session and return its redirect URL
Poll a checkout session's status after redirect

endpoints.notes: Signature verified on the raw body before parsing; always acknowledged quickly, processed in a job

endpoints.purpose: Signed link to the invoice PDF
Discrepancies between our records and the gateway

contract.name: payment.Gateway
contract.purpose: The adapter Strategy interface; internal to this module

dependsWhy.subscription: Knows what is being purchased and what a successful payment should activate
dependsWhy.job: Webhook processing, dunning and reconciliation run asynchronously

rules: Card data never reaches our servers. Checkout is hosted by the gateway; we hold only tokens and identifiers.
Webhook signatures are verified against the **raw** body before any parsing. An unverified webhook is logged and rejected.
Webhook processing is idempotent on `provider_event_id`; a duplicate is acknowledged without reprocessing.
Webhooks are acknowledged within 2 seconds and processed in a job — a slow handler causes the gateway to retry and duplicate.
Every webhook is stored raw, so it can be replayed after a bug fix without asking the gateway to resend.
Checkout creation requires an `Idempotency-Key`; a network retry must not create a second session or a second charge.
The gateway is the source of truth for whether money moved; our records are reconciled against it daily, and a discrepancy raises an alert rather than being auto-corrected.
Refunds require a reason and a permission, and are always audited.
Dunning follows a fixed schedule (day 1, 3, 5) with clear communications, and stops immediately on success.
Amounts are `numeric` with an explicit currency; floating point is never used for money anywhere in this module.
A payment failure never revokes access directly — it emits an event and `subscription` decides.

errors.meaning: Our record disagrees with the gateway

security: PCI scope is limited to the gateway's hosted fields; we never see, transmit, or store a card number.
Webhook endpoints are public by necessity and are therefore rate-limited, signature-verified and logged in full.
Refund and grant permissions are separate from general billing read access.
Every state change in this module is audited with the actor, and admin actions require a stated reason.
Two reviewers are required for any change to this module (rule S11).

flows.title: Checkout and activation
flows.mermaid:
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor U as Learner
    participant P as payment
    participant G as Gateway
    participant S as subscription
    participant M as mailer

    U->>P: POST /billing/checkout { plan } (Idempotency-Key)
    P->>S: validate the plan is purchasable for this learner
    P->>G: create hosted session
    G-->>P: session id + redirect URL
    P->>P: INSERT checkout_sessions
    P-->>U: { redirect_url }
    U->>G: completes payment on the gateway's page
    G->>P: webhook payment.succeeded
    P->>P: verify signature on the raw body
    P->>P: store raw webhook; ack 200 immediately
    P->>P: enqueue processing job
    Note over P: processing is idempotent on provider_event_id
    P->>P: INSERT payments, invoices; generate the PDF
    P->>S: publish payment.succeeded
    S->>S: activate the subscription; invalidate entitlements
    P->>M: receipt email
    U->>P: GET /billing/checkout/{id} → completed

flows.title: Failed renewal and dunning
flows.mermaid:
flowchart TD A[Renewal charge fails] --> B[publish payment.failed] B --> C[subscription enters Grace, access continues] C --> D[dunning day 1: email] D --> E{recovered?} E -->|yes| F[payment.succeeded → Active] E -->|no| G[dunning day 3: email + in-app] G --> H{recovered?} H -->|yes| F H -->|no| I[dunning day 5: final notice] I --> J{recovered?} J -->|yes| F J -->|no| K[grace expires → Free
no data deleted]

tasks.title: Add a payment provider
steps: Implement `payment.Gateway` in `gateway/<provider>/`; the SDK may be imported only there.
Implement signature verification against the raw body, and test it with a forged payload.
Map the provider's event names onto our internal event set.
Add sandbox credentials for CI and a fixture set covering success, decline, timeout and duplicate webhook.
Run the reconciliation job against the sandbox.
Get a second reviewer — this module requires two (rule S11).

limitations: No tax or VAT calculation in v1; prices are tax-inclusive and this is stated at checkout.
No dunning personalisation beyond the fixed schedule.
Invoice PDFs are generated from a simple template with no localisation beyond currency formatting.
Reconciliation is daily, so a discrepancy can persist for up to a day before it is visible.
testFocus: Webhook signature verification rejects a forged or replayed-with-changes payload
Duplicate webhook produces exactly one payment record
Idempotent checkout creation under a network retry
Refund partial and full, with window enforcement
Reconciliation detects a seeded discrepancy
Money arithmetic never uses floating point (asserted by a lint rule and a test)
A payment failure does not itself revoke access
coverage: 90% service (money-handling code carries the highest correctness bar in the repository)

decisions.question: Hosted checkout or our own card form?
decisions.why: It keeps PCI scope to SAQ-A, removes an entire class of liability, and the conversion difference does not justify the risk

decisions.question: Trust webhooks or poll?
decisions.why: Webhooks are timely but can be missed or duplicated; daily reconciliation against the gateway catches both without polling constantly

decisions.question: Store raw webhooks?
decisions.why: Replay after a bug fix is the difference between a five-minute recovery and asking a payment provider to resend a week of events

decisions.question: Who decides access after a payment?
decisions.why: Keeping the money boundary separate from the access boundary means a gateway problem cannot silently change what learners can do

openQuestions: Which gateway — VNPay/MoMo for Vietnam, Stripe for international, or both behind the adapter? (plan review Q1)

todo.title: Phase 4
items: Gateway interface and the first adapter
Hosted checkout session creation with idempotency
Webhook endpoint with raw-body signature verification and fast acknowledgement
Refunds with window and permission enforcement
Daily reconciliation job with discrepancy alerts

doNot: Do not accept or store card data.
Do not parse a webhook before verifying its signature on the raw body.
Do not process a webhook synchronously in the request.
Do not use floating point for money.
Do not revoke access from this module — publish an event.
Do not auto-correct a reconciliation discrepancy; raise it.
